post.summary: Apply a batch of atomic operations
post.description: Applies an ordered batch of write operations all-or-nothing within a single transaction (the JSON:API Atomic Operations extension). Negotiated via the `ext="https://jsonapi.org/ext/atomic"` media-type parameter on both the request `Content-Type` and the `Accept` header. Either every operation is committed or none is; a failure rolls the whole batch back. The batch commits through a single transactional persister.

requestBody.description: The batch of operations. Sent under the extension-qualified `application/vnd.api+json; ext="https://jsonapi.org/ext/atomic"` media type.

200.description: The result of each operation, in batch order.

400.description: Bad Request — the operations document was malformed.

404.description: Not Found — an operation targets a resource that does not exist.

406.description: Not Acceptable — the `Accept` header did not request the atomic extension.

409.description: Conflict — an operation conflicts with the resource state (e.g. a type or id mismatch).

415.description: Unsupported Media Type — the `Content-Type` did not carry the atomic `ext` parameter.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity — an operation in the batch failed validation. The whole batch is rolled back.

AccessDeniedError.title: Forbidden
AccessDeniedError.description: The caller is authenticated but not permitted to do what the request asks. Retrying with the same credentials will fail the same way; act as a user who holds the permission, or don't make the request.

AdditionProhibitedError.title: Addition is prohibited
AdditionProhibitedError.description: This relationship does not let a client add members to it. Don't retry the request; the relationship changes only in the ways the API documents for it.

ApplicationError.title: Application error
ApplicationError.description: The server failed to handle the request because of a fault on its side, not because of anything in the request. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.

lid.description: A local id assigned to the created resource, referenceable by later operations in the batch.

ArticlesAtomicUpdate.description: The article resource object an `update` operation writes.

lid.description: The local id of a resource created earlier in the batch.

oneOf.title: Targeted by ref/href
oneOf.description: Neither `id` nor `lid` in `data` — the operation targets the resource by its `ref` or `href`.

AtomicOperation.description: One operation in the batch. The target is given by exactly one of `ref` or `href`.

ref.description: A structural reference to the operation's target (an alternative to `href`). Identifies a resource by `type` plus exactly one of `id` or `lid`; `relationship` narrows the target to that relationship.

lid.description: A local id referencing a resource created earlier in the same batch.

href.description: A URI reference to the operation's target (an alternative to `ref`).

data.description: The operation payload. Its shape depends on `op` and the target: a resource object for an `add`/`update`; a resource identifier (or `null`) for a to-one relationship; an array of resource identifiers for a to-many relationship; absent for a resource `remove`.

AtomicOperationsInvalidError.title: Atomic operations request is invalid
AtomicOperationsInvalidError.description: An operation in the Atomic Operations request is malformed: a missing or unknown `op`, or a broken `ref`, `href` or `data`. The server applied none of the batch; fix the operation at `source.pointer` and send the whole batch again.

AtomicOperationsRequest.description: The Atomic Operations extension request document: an ordered, all-or-nothing batch of write operations.

atomic:operations.description: The ordered list of operations to apply. Applied in array order, all-or-nothing within one transaction.

AtomicResult.description: The result fragment of one operation. It carries only `data` and `meta`, and a `remove` returns it empty.

data.description: The created or updated resource (or its identifier) the operation returns.

AtomicResultsResponse.description: The Atomic Operations extension response document: one result fragment per applied operation, in batch order.

atomic:results.description: The result of each operation, in batch order.

AttributeValueInvalidError.title: Attribute value is invalid
AttributeValueInvalidError.description: The server could not accept the value of the attribute at `source.pointer`, for example a date-time it cannot parse. Correct the value and send the request again.

detail.example: The value for attribute "publishedAt" is invalid: Failed to parse time string (next blursday) at position 0 (n): The timezone could not be found in the database

AuthenticationRequiredError.title: Unauthorized
AuthenticationRequiredError.description: The request carried no credentials, or credentials the server rejected, such as an expired token. Authenticate, then send the request again with valid credentials.

ClientGeneratedIdAlreadyExistsError.title: Client generated ID already exists
ClientGeneratedIdAlreadyExistsError.description: A resource of this type already has the `id` the create request supplied. Generate a new id and send the request again, or update the existing resource instead.

ClientGeneratedIdNotSupportedError.title: Client generated ID is not supported
ClientGeneratedIdNotSupportedError.description: The create request supplied an `id`, but this resource type assigns its own ids. Leave `data.id` out and the server generates one.

ClientGeneratedIdRequiredError.title: Required client generated ID
ClientGeneratedIdRequiredError.description: This resource type expects the client to choose the id, and the create request supplied none. Add `data.id` in the format the API documents and send the request again.

CursorMalformedError.title: Cursor is malformed
CursorMalformedError.description: The cursor in the named `page` parameter could not be decoded. Use cursors exactly as the server returned them in a previous page's `links`; never build or edit one.

CursorStaleError.title: Cursor is stale
CursorStaleError.description: The cursor was issued for a different sort order than this request asks for, so it no longer marks a position in these results. Keep `sort` unchanged while paging, or start again from the first page.

DataMemberMissingError.title: Missing `data` member at the document's top level
DataMemberMissingError.description: The request document has no top-level `data` member, which this request needs. Send the resource object or relationship linkage under `data`.

Send a JSON:API document as `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` with only the parameters the server supports.

QueryParamUnrecognizedError.title: Query parameter is unrecognized
QueryParamUnrecognizedError.description: The request used a query parameter this endpoint does not recognize. Remove it, or check its spelling against the parameters the API documents.

RelatedAttributeOwnerMissingError.title: Related attribute owner missing
RelatedAttributeOwnerMissingError.description: The request wrote an attribute the server stores on a related resource, and that related resource does not exist. Set the relationship first, or leave the attribute out.

detail.example: Cannot write attribute "city": its related "address" is not present.

RelationshipCountNotAllowedError.title: Relationship count is not allowed
RelationshipCountNotAllowedError.description: `withCount` names a relationship that is not a countable to-many relationship of this resource. Ask for counts only on the relationships the API marks as countable.

RelationshipNotExistsError.title: The requested relationship does not exist!
RelationshipNotExistsError.description: The request names a relationship this resource type does not have, or one whose endpoint the API does not expose. Check the relationship name against the ones the type documents.

RelationshipTypeInappropriateError.title: Relationship type is inappropriate
RelationshipTypeInappropriateError.description: The relationship data has the wrong cardinality: a list for a to-one relationship, a single identifier for a to-many one, or a `POST` or `DELETE` to a to-one relationship endpoint. Send linkage that matches the relationship.

detail.example: The provided relationship 'author' is of type of to-many, but to-one is expected!

RemovalProhibitedError.title: Removal is prohibited
RemovalProhibitedError.description: This relationship does not let a client remove members from it or clear it. Don't retry the request; the relationship changes only in the ways the API documents for it.

RenderedLink.description: A link the server builds, rendered as a JSON:API link object. `describedby` is a URI-reference to the OpenAPI operation that describes the link's target, present when the server describes its links.

RequestBodyInvalidJsonApiError.title: Request body is an invalid JSON:API document
RequestBodyInvalidJsonApiError.description: The request body is JSON but breaks the JSON:API document structure or the schema the server validates this resource against. Each violation is its own error, with `source.pointer` set where the server could locate it.

RequestBodyInvalidJsonError.title: Request body is an invalid JSON document
RequestBodyInvalidJsonError.description: The request body is not well-formed JSON. Fix the syntax the `detail` reports and send the request again.

RequiredTopLevelMembersMissingError.title: Required top-level members are missing
RequiredTopLevelMembersMissingError.description: The request body is not a JSON object, or has none of the top-level members `data`, `errors` and `meta`. Send a JSON object with the resource under `data`.

ResourceIdConflictError.title: Resource id conflict
ResourceIdConflictError.description: The `id` in the update body is not the `id` in the URL. Send the id of the resource the URL addresses as `data.id`.

detail.example: Resource id '12' does not match the endpoint id '7'!

ResourceIdInvalidError.title: Resource ID is invalid
ResourceIdInvalidError.description: The resource object's `id` is not a string, such as a number. Send `data.id` as a JSON string.

ResourceIdMissingError.title: Resource ID is missing
ResourceIdMissingError.description: The update request's resource object has no `id`. Include the id of the resource being updated as `data.id`.

ResourceIdUndecodableError.title: Resource ID is undecodable
ResourceIdUndecodableError.description: The client-generated `id` is not in a format the server can decode into one of its own ids. Send an `id` in the format the API documents for this resource type.

ResourceIdentifierIdInvalidError.title: Resource identifier ID is invalid
ResourceIdentifierIdInvalidError.description: A resource identifier in the request carries an `id` that is not a string, such as a number. Send every `id` as a JSON string.

ResourceIdentifierIdMissingError.title: An ID for the resource identifier is missing
ResourceIdentifierIdMissingError.description: A resource identifier in the request has neither an `id` nor a `lid`. Identify each related resource by its `id`, or by a `lid` inside an Atomic Operations request.

ResourceIdentifierLidInvalidError.title: Resource identifier local ID is invalid
ResourceIdentifierLidInvalidError.description: A resource identifier in the request carries a `lid` that is not a string. Send every `lid` as a JSON string.

ResourceIdentifierTypeInvalidError.title: Resource identifier type is invalid
ResourceIdentifierTypeInvalidError.description: A resource identifier in the request carries a `type` that is not a string. Send every `type` as a JSON string.

ResourceIdentifierTypeMissingError.title: A type for the resource identifier is missing
ResourceIdentifierTypeMissingError.description: A resource identifier in the request has no `type`. Add the related resource's `type` to every identifier.

ResourceNotFoundError.title: Resource not found
ResourceNotFoundError.description: The resource the request addresses does not exist. Check the type and id in the URL; a deleted resource stays not found.

ResourceTypeMissingError.title: Resource type is missing
ResourceTypeMissingError.description: The resource object in `data` has no `type`. Add the type of the resource the endpoint serves.

ResourceTypeUnacceptableError.title: Resource type is unacceptable
ResourceTypeUnacceptableError.description: The `type` in the request is not one this endpoint or relationship accepts. Send the type the endpoint serves, or one the relationship documents for its related resources.

ResponseBodyInvalidJsonApiError.title: Response body is an invalid JSON:API document
ResponseBodyInvalidJsonApiError.description: The server produced a response that breaks the JSON:API document structure, which is a fault on its side. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.

ResponseBodyInvalidJsonError.title: Response body is an invalid JSON document
ResponseBodyInvalidJsonError.description: The server produced a response body that is not valid JSON, which is a fault on its side. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.

SortingUnrecognizedError.title: Sorting parameter is unrecognized
SortingUnrecognizedError.description: The `sort` parameter names a field this endpoint cannot sort by. Sort only on the fields the API documents for this resource type.

detail.example: Sorting parameter 'popularity' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

SortingUnsupportedError.title: Sorting is unsupported
SortingUnsupportedError.description: This endpoint does not support sorting. Remove the `sort` parameter.

relatedQuery.name: relatedQuery
relatedQuery.description: Per-relationship sort and filter applied from the primary request, addressed by relationship (include) path (the Relationship Queries profile). e.g. `relatedQuery[author][sort]=-createdAt` or `relatedQuery[comments][filter][state]=open`. Recognised only when the Relationship Queries profile is negotiated.

sort.description: A comma-separated list of sort fields for the addressed relationship; prefix a field with `-` for descending order.

filter.description: A `filter[<key>]=<value>` map applied to the addressed relationship, in the same shape as the primary `filter`.
